# cancho-web

> cancho-web makes the API boundary a checked artifact of the program. A web layer for cancho, a typed systems language whose compiler states what a program may touch (`cancho authority`: for the users service, no files and no foreign code): each operation (route, parameters, body, responses) is declared once, and the router and an OpenAPI 3.1 document are made from that declaration. Request bodies are validated by cancho-schema, every error at once, as RFC 9457 problem+json. One thread, no Ffi, no C. Alpha: the declaration, parameter dispatch and bearer-token authorization (`web.guard`) are built; dependency injection, OAuth, a request id, CORS, rate limiting and defaults declared once are not, and no service here is put behind TLS.

## Read first
- [Overview](https://alpibrusl.github.io/cancho-web/): what it is, where it fits, the numbers.
- [Examples](https://alpibrusl.github.io/cancho-web/examples.html): the users API run, with the answers it gives and the document it serves.
- [Evidence](https://alpibrusl.github.io/cancho-web/evidence.html): what the tests cover, what building it found, how each benchmark number was measured, what is not claimed.
- [Design](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-web/blob/main/docs/design.md): what the framework layer is, what building the example found, and what is next.
- [Benchmarks](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-web/blob/main/docs/benchmarks.md): the method and the tables, against FastAPI, Go net/http, Go fasthttp, Rust axum and a hand-written C server, and on PostgreSQL.

## Facts that matter when using it
- The application keeps its own loop (`server.wait`, `server.next`, `server.respond`) and matches on the route id `web.find` returns; a framework that owned the loop would need handlers to be handed a view of buffers they cannot name a region for, which does not type-check in cancho today.
- `web.operation` registers a route and answers its id; `path_param`, `query_param`, `header_param`, `body`, `respond`, `respond_problem` declare the rest. The same declaration writes the OpenAPI document (`web.openapi`), which is checked in as `examples/users/openapi.json`.
- `web.dispatch` is called in the application's loop where `web.find` was. For a request with a route and valid path, query and header parameters it answers the route id and fills a slot table (`web.slot`, `web.int_arg`, `web.present`); otherwise it writes the 404, 405 or 422 itself (every error, at `/query/limit`, `/path/id`, `/header/Name`, with a code) and answers `web.answered()`, so the handler is not reached. Values are judged decoded; an unknown or repeated query key is refused for an operation that declares query parameters.
- Bodies: `cancho-schema` returns every error with a JSON Pointer; no coercion (`"3"` is not an integer; `150.0` is). Errors are `application/problem+json`.
- Who may call an operation (`bearer_scheme`, `require`, `no_auth`) is written to the document, can be read back (`requirements`, `requirement`, `is_open`) and is enforced by `web.guard(heap, api, tokens, request, table, id, out, keep)`, called after `web.dispatch`: no bearer credential is a 401 (`WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`), an unknown secret a 401 `invalid_token`, a secret held for another scheme a 403 `insufficient_scope`, any one of an operation's alternatives opens it, an operation the document lists nothing for is open. Credentials are data (`web.tokens_empty`, `web.token(heap, tokens, scheme, secret)`), not a callback. `web.bearer`, `web.unauthorized` and `web.forbidden` let an application do its own verification. `web.log_line` formats `METHOD path status milliseconds` (no query string). Example: `examples/guarded`.
- Benchmarks are one VM, one run: on one core 14-18x FastAPI and 1.3-1.4x Go net/http, ahead of a hand-written C server on a read and a page and 6-11% behind it on the rest; on two cores each, 19-25x FastAPI's two workers. In a later run on a slower VM, Go's fasthttp was faster than cancho on a read (80,150 against 72,153 a second) and a create (45,428 against 42,562), cancho was ahead on a page of 20 and level on a rejected body, and cancho was 1.3-1.8x ahead of Rust axum on one thread. Resident memory at rest is 1.8 MiB and start-up 4 ms (FastAPI lean: 47 MiB and 486 ms; Go net/http 7.4 MiB; the hand-written C server 1.8 MiB, 6.7 MiB with 100 idle connections, cancho 2.0 MiB). A first run on a faster VM had 15-26x: a ratio against a Python program depends on the machine.

## Not built
Dependency injection, OAuth/sessions/expiry, a request id, CORS, rate limiting, defaults declared once. (`web.dispatch` is in all three services: users, users_pg, users_threads.)

## In cancho, not used here
cancho has a TLS 1.3 server (not independently reviewed) and an http.server that a terminator can drive (examples/https_hello): no service in this repository has been put behind it, so terminate TLS in front. cancho has threads: examples/users_threads runs the loop in two, each with its own store (not a deployable service). http.server can stream a response: web cannot declare one yet.
